A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TGMM study and provide readable main text, figures, equations, and complete appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic GMM experiments comparing TGMM with classical algorithms, alongside distribution-shift tests and architecture analyses in Section 3 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and results in Section 3 and Appendix H, including isotropic and anisotropic GMM evaluation.

M1.justification: The task embeddings, shared transformer, task-specific readouts, and meta-training objectives are unchanged. The Mamba2 backbone and anisotropic extensions already appear in v1; relocated definitions do not introduce new components.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same synthetic isotropic and anisotropic GMM tasks, component counts, dimensions, sample-size shifts, and perturbed mean distributions. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain EM and spectral methods for isotropic tasks, EM for anisotropic tasks, and transformer versus Mamba2 backbones. Newly cited density-estimation methods are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 retains the 12-layer, four-head, 128-dimensional default backbone, one million training steps, and 1,280 evaluation tasks. Data generation, parameter matching, evaluation metrics, and appendix ablation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The sample-size and mean-perturbation robustness tests, backbone width/depth analyses, and Mamba2 readout comparison are retained. The new fairness remark adds discussion rather than an experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Averaging over 1,280 sampled tasks and the plotted error bars are unchanged. v2 adds no seed information, repeated-run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The result plots in Figures 2–6 and 10–17 retain identical graphical content and result series. Reported findings, including the high-dimensional log-likelihood disadvantage discussed in the empirical appendix, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The EM approximation assumptions, bounds, constructions, and proofs match across Appendices C and F; the tensor results match across Appendices D and G. The new layer-efficiency comparison highlights an existing bound rather than revising the mathematics.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly adds an O(L)-versus-O(KL) layer-efficiency claim relative to He et al. (2025b). Its expanded conclusion also refers broadly to implementing spectral methods, whereas the retained guarantee concerns their cubic tensor iteration component.

C2.justification: New Remark 1 addresses comparison fairness by characterizing meta-training's additional information as distributional knowledge and invoking the existing generalization results. Section 5 adds an interpretation of TGMM performance as interpolating between EM and spectral methods. Existing limitations largely move to Appendix E.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses LLM assistance in drafting preliminary code snippets. Hyperparameters, software libraries, eight 80 GB A100 GPUs, and code-access statements remain unchanged; the disclosure does not establish an implementation change.

R1.justification: New Appendix A discusses density-estimation work by Liu et al. (2025), Schaeffer et al. (2024), and Fakoor et al. (2020). The introduction expands the existing comparison with He et al. (2025b), particularly regarding layer complexity.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion receive limited revisions. Full network definitions move to Appendix C and limitations to Appendix E, while most exposition remains intact. Appendix F.2 introduces an unresolved '??' reference where v1 referenced its encoding equation.

P2.justification: v2 adopts ICLR headers, title and heading styles, and revised page composition, with some equations and figures reflowed. The single-column structure and graphical content of all 17 figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The expanded research positioning and fairness discussion provide useful context. However, v2 introduces an unresolved reference in Appendix F.2 and less qualified wording about implementing spectral methods in Section 5, despite Appendix E retaining full spectral approximation as future work. With the technical evidence preserved, these limited contextual gains and losses in precision leave the net quality direction uncertain.
